Topics · The holy books together

Which commandment did Jesus call the first?

Jesus began with Israel's oldest confession, and the Quran's Jesus stands the same way. What does that show?

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَمُصَدِّقًا لِّمَا بَيْنَ يَدَىَّ مِنَ ٱلتَّوْرَىٰةِ وَلِأُحِلَّ لَكُم بَعْضَ ٱلَّذِى حُرِّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ ۚ وَجِئْتُكُم بِـَٔايَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّكُمْ فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ٥٠ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ رَبِّى وَرَبُّكُمْ فَٱعْبُدُوهُ ۗ هَـٰذَا صِرَٰطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ٥١﴾

Translation of the meaning

And [I have come] confirming what was before me of the Torah and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you. And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so fear Allāh and obey me. Indeed, Allāh is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. That is the straight path.'"

Quran · Aal Imran 3:50-51

Translation

“Don’t think that I came to destroy the law or the prophets. I didn’t come to destroy, but to fulfill.

Original · Ancient Greek

Μὴ νομίσητε ὅτι ἦλθον καταλῦσαι τὸν νόμον ἢ τοὺς προφήτας· οὐκ ἦλθον καταλῦσαι ἀλλὰ πληρῶσαι·

the Gospel (Matthew) · 5:17

World English Bible

Mark's Gospel records that when a scribe asked Jesus which commandment stands first, he began with the confession that the Lord is one, and only then spoke of love. A first answer shows what everything else rests on. The Quran gives him the same stance: he comes confirming the Torah before him, and his own sentence names one Lord over himself and his hearers.

A question for you

Why do you think he began there, when he could have begun anywhere?

If you sayIt was the foundation, and he came to confirm it
ThenThen the first thing Jesus taught was something he had received, and he stood under it beside the scribe. The next question is how far back that confession goes.
If you sayHe was meeting Jews in their own language
ThenA good teacher does that. Yet he was asked what comes first, and whoever answers that question says what he holds to be first. Whatever else he meant, he put this at the head of the list.
If you sayIt was the start, and its fullness came with him
ThenMany Christians read it this way: the confession stands, the Church confesses one God in three persons, and Jesus himself is within that one God. The confession is kept and its meaning deepened. Carry that reading with you into what follows.

Part 2 of 3

﴿أَمْ كُنتُمْ شُهَدَآءَ إِذْ حَضَرَ يَعْقُوبَ ٱلْمَوْتُ إِذْ قَالَ لِبَنِيهِ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنۢ بَعْدِى قَالُوا۟ نَعْبُدُ إِلَـٰهَكَ وَإِلَـٰهَ ءَابَآئِكَ إِبْرَٰهِـۧمَ وَإِسْمَـٰعِيلَ وَإِسْحَـٰقَ إِلَـٰهًا وَٰحِدًا وَنَحْنُ لَهُۥ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Or were you witnesses when death approached Jacob, when he said to his sons, "What will you worship after me?" They said, "We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Ishmael and Isaac - one God.[46] And we are Muslims [in submission] to Him."

Translator's notes

[46] Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) alone.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:133

Translation

Jacob called to his sons, and said: “Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which will happen to you in the days to come. Assemble yourselves, and hear, you sons of Jacob. Listen to Israel, your father.

Original · Hebrew

וַיִּקְרָ֥א יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֶל־בָּנָ֑יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֵאָֽסְפוּ֙ וְאַגִּ֣ידָה לָכֶ֔ם אֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר־יִקְרָ֥א אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּאַחֲרִ֥ית הַיָּמִֽים׃ הִקָּבְצ֥וּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ בְּנֵ֣י יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְשִׁמְע֖וּ אֶל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל אֲבִיכֶֽם׃

the Torah (Genesis) · 49:1-2

World English Bible

The confession is older than Moses's hearers. The verse shows Jacob, who is Israel, as death comes near, asking his sons one thing: what will you worship after me? They answer with one God, the God of their fathers. If that is so, what Israel confesses had once been a family's promise to a dying father. That changes what Jesus was doing when he put it first. He was standing in a line, and everyone in that line faces the same way.

A question for you

In Mark the scribe gives the answer back: God is one, and there is no other. What did Jesus say to him then?

If you sayThat he was not far from the kingdom of God
ThenThen what brought this man near the kingdom, in this scene, was his confession that God is one and that loving Him outweighs every offering. Christians will say the rest of the Gospel covers the remaining distance, and that deserves weighing. Notice what drew those words to him.
If you sayThat he still lacked something
ThenYou might expect that, since the Gospel has a nearby scene with a rich young man. With this scribe the words are warmer. Compare the two scenes and look at what that warmth rested on here.
If you sayI do not remember
ThenThe answer is worth finding for yourself. The passage comes after this Step, with others from your own book.

Part 3 of 3

﴿شَرَعَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلدِّينِ مَا وَصَّىٰ بِهِۦ نُوحًا وَٱلَّذِىٓ أَوْحَيْنَآ إِلَيْكَ وَمَا وَصَّيْنَا بِهِۦٓ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ وَمُوسَىٰ وَعِيسَىٰٓ ۖ أَنْ أَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلدِّينَ وَلَا تَتَفَرَّقُوا۟ فِيهِ ۚ كَبُرَ عَلَى ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ مَا تَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَيْهِ ۚ ٱللَّهُ يَجْتَبِىٓ إِلَيْهِ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهْدِىٓ إِلَيْهِ مَن يُنِيبُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

He has ordained for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah and that which We have revealed to you, [O Muḥammad], and what We enjoined upon Abraham and Moses and Jesus - to establish the religion and not be divided therein. Difficult for those who associate others with Allāh is that to which you invite them. Allāh chooses for Himself whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back [to Him].

Quran · Ash-Shura 42:13

﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا نُوحِىٓ إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَـٰهَ إِلَّآ أَنَا۠ فَٱعْبُدُونِ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And We sent not before you any messenger except We revealed to him that, "There is no deity except Me, so worship Me."

Quran · Al-Anbiya 21:25

Translation

I am Yahweh, and there is no one else. Besides me, there is no God. I will strengthen you, though you have not known me,

Original · Hebrew

אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ וְאֵ֣ין ע֔וֹד זוּלָתִ֖י אֵ֣ין אֱלֹהִ֑ים אֲאַזֶּרְךָ֖ וְלֹ֥א יְדַעְתָּֽנִי׃

Isaiah · 45:5

World English Bible

If one sender stands behind them all, the first instruction should match across the centuries, and that can be checked. The first verse names Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus, along with the one it addresses, and gives them one charge: establish the religion and do not split over it. The second widens the circle to every messenger. On this account Jesus's beginning is what one would expect. He said what he was sent to say, as each before him had.

A question for you

The church says God is one, the synagogue says it, and the Quran says it. What would you most want to ask next?

If you sayWhat the word one means
ThenThat is where the conversation belongs. 3:51 gives a plain place to begin: the speaker calls God his own Lord as well as yours. Ask what the words my Lord can mean on the lips of the one who says them.
If you sayWho Jesus is
ThenThen hold on to the sentence that is shared. The Quran's way is to begin from it and weigh every other question in its light.
If you sayWhat people did with it afterwards
ThenA generous answer, and a searching one. The verse forbids splitting and treats it as people's own work. Muslims read that warning about their own divisions too.

The same in the other books

Now therefore, Yahweh our God, save us, I beg you, out of his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you, Yahweh, are God alone.”

Your reflection

If someone asked you for the one sentence everything else in your faith rests on, what would you say, and who taught it to you?
